RUNTIME: raw-evidence-index hashes all match the frozen solution bytes. workspace.json reports 21 scripted golden groups with passed:true, covering transitions, places, stale/who, roles, undo/reopen, bulk all-or-none/board order/mixed stages/reorder-blocks-undo (workspace.cjs:125-179), privacy, paging, unread/seen, live board with draft/focus, scroll-place, session resume, observer, restart, and no page errors. COUNTEREXAMPLE PROBES: (a) Weak app that could pass: a client that only hides skip/Hired-reject controls is defeated by the replay steps in hro_move_one_stage/hro_reject_hired, so the golden's server checks are what is graded. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: an app whose undo Activity line names only the destination stage. The golden itself writes 'X undid a move: Y is back in Applied' (index.js:366) and gives no from-stage; a strict reading of hro_activity 'naming who and what changed (the stages for moves)' could in principle penalise it. I judge it plausibly satisfying (who, card and resulting stage are stated; undo is listed separately from moves), but it is a judge-interpretation risk. (c) Transient: when a message arrives while the conversation is open at the newest message, update() briefly renders the server unread (+1) on the row and the nav total before catchUp/markRead and the follow-up SSE refresh clear it (threads.js:203-213; app.js:115-121). The protocol reads at or after 15 s, so the steady state is correct, but an early snapshot could see the blip. WHY RISK=TRUE: The workbook wants the oracle to be able to score high.
